name: Infant-type Hemispheric Glioma ALK-altered
aliases: Infantile Hemispheric Glioma with ALK Fusion

criteria.description: Presence of high-grade glioma histopathological features in hemispheric brain tissue
Detection of ALK gene fusion or rearrangement by molecular genetic testing
Onset in infancy or early childhood (typically under 2 years of age)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of hemispheric glioma combined with molecular evidence of ALK gene fusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology and molecular genetic testing per WHO CNS tumor classification.

searchTerms: rapid onset of focal nerve problems
fast progression of localized brain deficits

pathognomonic.symptomName: Seizures localized to affected cerebral hemisphere

searchTerms: headache and vomiting from brain swelling
weakness on one side of body
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction caused by brain lesion

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to tumor mass effect
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from tumor
excess brain fluid due to mass

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI showing large, unilateral hemispheric mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Peritumoral edema and mass effect on adjacent brain structures
genetic: ALK gene fusion or rearrangement detected by FISH, RT-PCR, or NGS
Absence of other common pediatric glioma mutations (e.g., BRAF V600E)
other: Histopathology consistent with high-grade glioma with astrocytic features
Immunohistochemistry positive for ALK protein expression

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of BRAF V600E mutation instead of ALK fusion
Tumor located in midline structures rather than hemispheric

redFlags: New onset focal seizures in infancy
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
Mackay A et al. Integrated molecular meta-analysis of 1,000 pediatric high-grade and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma. Cancer Cell. 2017
